drafts.title: Crossroads
drafts.reasoning: This scene focuses on the tension between two different law enforcement officers' methods of dealing with a case. Hank represents traditional policing tactics, while John embodies a more modern approach that emphasizes community engagement.
drafts.scene: The briefing room is dimly lit by flickering fluorescent lights. HANK sits at the head of a long table, scowling. JOHN stands next to him, hands in pockets, looking eager but slightly uneasy.

dialogue.line: You think you can just waltz into a crime scene like it’s some kind of charity event?
Hey, we need to talk to people. People are key witnesses here.
Witnesses get scared off when they see you handing out free chips and candy. It's about authority.
Free snacks have led to important tips before! Besides, we’re working together, right?
Right, because ‘working together’ doesn’t mean giving up your command presence.
Command presence is good for intimidation, not actually solving cases. We need actual information.
Information comes from fear and respect, not from bags of Doritos.
Doritos? Really, Captain? I thought you were the one who preferred Kevlar over common sense.
Kevlar has no taste, unlike my preference in coffee. And now, if you'll excuse me, I'm going to pretend none of this ever happened.
Well, it’s always fun to be underestimated. Except when it leads to a cold case.
That’s why we’re doing things the right way.
Oh yeah, because tradition and old-school tactics are known for clearing up crimes faster than ever before.
